title: OutpostCall
description: A call as the daemon sees it once it has opened the envelope with its sealing key (ADR 0148 §5, ADR 0149). Only `id` and `kind` are common to every kind: a daemon refuses a kind it does not know with `unsupported_kind`, and ignores a field it does not know. The call says nothing of whether the tool writes: the outpost reads that from its own server (ADR 0147 §6).

id.description: The call's id: the envelope's too, and the associated data it was sealed under. A daemon refuses `call_unreadable` a call whose id is not its envelope's.

kind.description: `call_tool` or `list_tools` in protocol 1 (`#/$defs/known_kind`). A later kind is refused `unsupported_kind` by a daemon that does not know it.

endpoint.description: The alias of an endpoint in the outpost's policy file.

tool.description: `call_tool`: the tool's name at the endpoint's server.

arguments.description: `call_tool`: the arguments, after the platform decided the call.

deadline.description: The door takes no answer after it, and the outpost makes no call after it; nothing a daemon sends moves it. A daemon judges it by its own clock: `server_time` is not signed, and may bring a deadline closer, never push it away. An RFC 3339 date-time that may carry a fraction of a second: the door writes it to the millisecond, never rounded past the lease it keeps, so that a call claimed late in its second does not reach the outpost up to a second short.

answer_key.description: The X25519 public key the answer is sealed to (raw, base64url without padding). It travels inside the envelope, where no proxy can rewrite it.

known_kind.description: The kinds of protocol 1: a tool call, and a tool listing (discovery).

asserted.description: Who the platform says the call is made for: the claims the gateway route signs (ADR 0149 §3). They are assertions of the control plane: an outpost may log them and decides nothing on them (ADR 0147 §6).

sub.description: The caller the platform acts for: a run, an action, a person.

org_id.description: The organisation's id, which survives a rename.

action.description: The governed action a write belongs to.

connector.description: The connector that routed the call.
